title: Offline bundle manifest schema + canonicalization rules for stable signatures
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Context
We need a signed offline bundle format for Redwood Private air-gapped installs. Signature verification must be stable across rebuilds and across toolchains (Go/Node/Python), otherwise customers will see intermittent failures (e.g., signature mismatch due to JSON formatting differences).

This ticket defines:
1) The manifest schema (fields + constraints + versioning)
2) Canonicalization rules used to produce the exact byte sequence that is signed
3) Deterministic ordering rules for lists/maps so that the signature is stable

Non-goals
- This ticket does not implement signing in CI or verification in the installer (tracked in ENG-4822/ENG-4823).
- This ticket does not finalize the signature envelope format (covered by ADR-0147), but must align with it.

Deliverables
- A manifest schema spec (human-readable) + example manifest
- Canonicalization spec (normative) and test vectors
- Clear constraints and rejection behavior for malformed/ambiguous manifests

Proposed decisions (to confirm during review)
- Manifest format: JSON (not YAML) to reduce canonicalization ambiguity.
- Canonicalization: RFC 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme / JCS) with additional Redwood constraints (see below) to simplify multi-language implementations.
- Hash algorithm for artifact entries: SHA-256 (hex lowercase) for all content digests; allow optional SHA-512 in the future but do not require now.
- Encoding: UTF-8, no BOM.

Manifest file name + location (bundle layout)
- <bundle_root>/manifest.json
- Detached signature stored separately (per ADR): <bundle_root>/manifest.sig
- Optional certificate chain / key id metadata stored as part of signature envelope (not in this ticket), but manifest must include key-agnostic fields only.

Schema: manifest.json (v1)
All fields are required unless noted.

Top-level
- schema_version (string): "redwood.offline_bundle.manifest.v1"
- bundle_format_version (string): semantic version of the offline bundle layout rules (e.g., "1.0.0"). Used to manage compatibility as we evolve directory structures.
- bundle_id (string): stable identifier for the bundle build; format "rb-priv-<private_release>-<build_id>" (see below). Not a UUID requirement but must be unique per published bundle.
- build_id (string): release pipeline build identifier (e.g., "2025.11.19.1+git.abc1234"). Must be stable and traceable.
- private_release (string): Redwood Private release version that installer expects (e.g., "2026.01.0").
- created_at_utc (string): RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC (e.g., "2025-11-19T02:14:22Z"). Note: included for provenance but does not drive ordering; must be produced deterministically from pipeline metadata.
- generated_by (string): tool name/version that generated the manifest (e.g., "redwood-bundler 0.9.3").
- source_commit (string): git sha for the bundling tool or monorepo release commit.
- requires_installer_version (string): minimum installer version required to verify/install this bundle (supports migration from unsigned bundles).

Security + downgrade/replay controls
- release_channel (string): "stable" | "rc" | "internal". Used by policy for what customers are allowed to install.
- monotonic_version (string): version string used for downgrade prevention, must compare deterministically. Proposed: reuse private_release, but allow build metadata; installer will compare (private_release, build_id) according to defined comparison rules (see Canonicalization + Comparison notes).

Artifacts
- artifacts (array): list of artifact entries. Must be sorted deterministically (see ordering rules).

Artifact entry (object)
- path (string): relative path within bundle using forward slashes (/). No leading "/". No ".." segments.
- type (string): enum
  - "installer_binary"
  - "helm_chart"
  - "container_image_tar"
  - "container_image_index"
  - "runtime_artifact"
  - "model_artifact"
  - "dependency_pkg"
  - "sbom"
  - "metadata"
- size_bytes (string): decimal integer as string (avoid JSON number ambiguity across languages). Example: "4839201".
- sha256 (string): lowercase hex string length 64.
- media_type (string, optional): e.g., "application/gzip", "application/x-tar", "application/vnd.cncf.helm.chart".
- version (string, optional): component version if applicable (chart version, installer version, etc.).

SBOM linkage (minimal requirement)
- sbom (string, optional): path reference to an SBOM artifact also present in artifacts (type "sbom"). If provided, must point to an artifact entry.
- sbom_sha256 (string, optional): sha256 digest for the SBOM file (redundant if SBOM is in artifacts; included to make lookups easier for tooling). If present, must match the referenced artifact sha256.

Metadata for support/debug (allowed but must be deterministic)
- annotations (object string->string, optional): free-form small map for debugging (e.g., "bundle_build_host": "releases-03"). Constraints: keys/values are strings, key length <= 64, value length <= 256, max 32 entries.

Disallowed/constraints
- No floats anywhere (JSON number type is disallowed at all; represent integers as strings).
- No nulls.
- No duplicate artifact paths.
- Total manifest size target: <= 512KB (hard fail above 2MB).

Canonicalization rules (normative)
We sign EXACT bytes of the canonicalized manifest JSON.

1) Parse
- Input manifest must parse as JSON object.
- Reject if any key appears twice at the same object level (duplicate member names).

2) Normalize data model constraints
- All numeric values must be represented as JSON strings containing only digits (0-9) (e.g., size_bytes). Reject JSON numbers.
- All hashes must be lowercase hex; reject uppercase.
- Paths must use "/" separators; reject "\\".

3) Canonical JSON serialization
- Use RFC 8785 (JCS) to produce canonical JSON bytes:
  - UTF-8 encoding
  - Object member names sorted lexicographically by Unicode code points
  - No insignificant whitespace
  - Escape rules per JCS

4) Additional Redwood ordering constraints
JCS only sorts object keys; it does not sort arrays. We must define array ordering for determinism.
- artifacts array MUST be sorted by:
  1. path (lexicographic)
  2. type (lexicographic)
  3. sha256 (lexicographic)
- If bundler generates artifacts in any other order, it must sort before writing.

5) Newline
- Canonicalized JSON MUST NOT include a trailing newline. The signed byte stream is exactly the canonical JSON bytes.

Comparison rules for downgrade prevention (note for ENG-4823)
- Installer should not implement free-form semver parsing of build_id. Proposal:
  - Compare private_release using semver (major, minor, patch).
  - If private_release equal, compare build_id lexicographically (pipeline ensures monotonicity) OR use created_at_utc as tie-breaker.
- Open question: created_at_utc inclusion can create non-reproducibility if not derived deterministically from pipeline metadata. If we cannot guarantee determinism, we should remove it or define it as pipeline build start time sourced from CI (stable per build).

Acceptance criteria
- Confluence spec updated with:
  - Full schema definition, required/optional fields
  - Deterministic ordering rules for arrays
  - Canonicalization rules + references to RFC 8785
  - At least 3 test vectors (example manifests + expected canonical bytes and sha256 of canonical bytes)
- Bundler and installer teams agree on:
  - Disallowed JSON number types (use strings)
  - Sorting rules for artifacts
  - Path normalization constraints
- Security review sign-off that canonicalization + schema prevents common ambiguity attacks (e.g., duplicate keys, whitespace tricks, array reordering).

Implementation notes / handoff
- Provide a tiny reference implementation (pseudo-code) for canonicalization + artifact sorting in the doc.
- Provide “golden” test fixtures for ENG-4823 to use in verification integration tests.

Open questions
1) Do we want to allow a second manifest encoding (CBOR) for future? (probably no for v1)
2) Should we embed an overall bundle sha256 for the tarball itself? (maybe separate; tarball hashing is transport-specific)
3) Should we allow multiple SBOMs? (e.g., per image) — can be represented as multiple artifacts of type sbom.

Risks
- If any field is produced nondeterministically (timestamps, hostnames), signatures will not be reproducible and will fail in re-packaging flows. We must be strict about what goes into manifest.
- If we allow JSON numbers, cross-language canonicalization will diverge (e.g., 1 vs 1.0). Hence the “no numbers” rule.

Rollout
- Start with schema_version v1 and enforce strict verification in installer for signed bundles.
- For migration from unsigned bundles, installer behavior is handled in ENG-4823/ENG-4824 (break-glass).
comments: 2025-11-01 (Marcus Lin): Strong +1 on RFC 8785, but must explicitly reject duplicate keys. Also recommend disallowing JSON numbers to avoid 1 vs 1.0 ambiguity. Add normative language about array ordering since JCS won’t cover that.

2025-11-04 (Connor O'Brien): Please make sure build_id format is pinned and comes from release tooling, not local timestamps. We need reproducible builds for evidence. Suggest: build_id = <private_release>.<release_train_counter>+git.<sha>.

2025-11-06 (Ethan Park): Installer implementation in Go: RFC 8785 libraries exist but vary in strictness. If we can provide test vectors and a minimal reference canonicalization routine, that will reduce integration bugs. Also, ensure path rules are strict (no backslashes, no ..).

2025-11-08 (Sahana Iyer): CI step can generate canonical bytes and publish sha256(canonical_bytes) as part of provenance. Please add explicit note: no trailing newline, UTF-8 no BOM. We saw newline differences in other pipelines.

2025-11-12 (Kevin Osei): For audit logging, we’ll want a stable manifest identifier: bundle_id + manifest sha256. Consider adding manifest_canonical_sha256 as a derived value (not signed) to logs; do not include it in manifest or you’ll create self-referential signing issues.

2025-11-18 (Jordan Lee): Updated spec: artifacts array sorting rules added; all numeric values are strings; added max manifest size guidance. Posted 3 test vectors in Confluence appendix and linked them for ENG-4823 integration tests.

2025-12-10 (Marcus Lin): Security sign-off contingent on: (1) duplicate key rejection, (2) path normalization rules, (3) strict hash formatting, (4) no JSON numbers. All addressed in latest revision. Approved.
resolution: Spec finalized and published in Confluence. Canonicalization based on RFC 8785 (JCS) with explicit array sorting + strict parsing constraints (no JSON numbers, reject duplicate keys). Test vectors provided for installer verification and CI signing steps. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-4822 (pipeline signing step) and ENG-4823 (installer preflight verification).
